Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-3217", "title": "Hantavirus Infections", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a rare viral infection caused by several strains of the hantavirus."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They shed the virus in their urine, droppings, and saliva."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Tiny droplets with the virus can enter the air."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "You can get the disease if you breathe infected air or come into contact with rodents or their urine or droppings."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Most of the time, you can't get the virus from another person."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "But one strain of the virus found in South America, called the Andes virus, spreads through close contact with someone who has the virus."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Early symptoms of HPS include: Fatigue Fever Muscle aches, especially in the thighs, hips, and back Headaches Chills Dizziness Nausea, vomiting , diarrhea or abdominal (belly) pain Later symptoms include coughing and shortness of breath ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Controlling rodents in and around your house is the best way to prevent infection."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "If you have been around rodents and have symptoms of fever, deep muscle aches, and severe shortness of breath, see your health care provider immediately."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "There is no specific treatment, cure, or vaccine for HPS."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-4", "title": "Diabetes", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Diabetes, also known as diabetes mellitus, is a disease in which your blood glucose , or blood sugar, levels are too high."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Glucose is your body's main source of energy."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your body can make glucose, but it also comes from the food you eat."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Insulin is a hormone made by your pancreas."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Insulin helps move glucose from your bloodstream into your cells, where it can be used for energy."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "If you have diabetes, your body can't make insulin, can't use insulin as well as it should, or both."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Too much glucose stays in your blood and doesn't reach your cells."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "This can cause glucose levels to get too high."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Over time, high blood glucose levels can lead to serious health conditions ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "But you can take steps to manage your diabetes and try to prevent these health problems."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "There are different types of diabetes: Type 1 diabetes ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "If you have type 1 diabetes, your body makes little or no insulin."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "It happens when your immune system attacks and destroys the cells that produce insulin."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "This is the most common form of diabetes."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "If you have type 2 diabetes, your body may still be able to make insulin, but your cells don't respond well to insulin."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "They can't easily take up enough glucose from your blood."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "This is a form of diabetes that develops during pregnancy."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It happens when your body can't make the extra insulin it needs during pregnancy."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The different types of diabetes have different causes: Researchers think type 1 diabetes is caused by genes and factors in the environment that might trigger the disease."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Type 2 diabetes is caused by several factors, including lifestyle factors and genes ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "The lifestyle factors include not being physically active and being overweight or having obesity ."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Researchers think gestational diabetes is caused by the hormonal changes of pregnancy along with genetic and lifestyle factors."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "The different types of diabetes have different risk factors: You can develop type 1 diabetes at any age, but it most often starts in childhood."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Having a parent or sibling with type 1 diabetes may increase your chance of developing it."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "You are at higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes if you: Are overweight or have obesity."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Children, teenagers, and younger adults can get diabetes, but it is more common in middle-aged and older adults."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "This means that your blood glucose is higher than normal, but it's not high enough to be called diabetes."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Have given birth to a baby weighing 9 pounds or more."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Are African American, American Indian, Asian American, Hispanic/Latino, or Pacific Islander."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Have certain other health conditions, such as high blood pressure or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "You are at higher risk of developing gestational diabetes if you: Are overweight or have obesity."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Had gestational diabetes in a previous pregnancy."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Have given birth to a baby weighing 9 pounds or more."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Are African American, Hispanic/Latino, American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, or Pacific Islander."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "The symptoms of diabetes may include: Feeling very thirsty Feeling very hungry Urinating (peeing) more often, including at night Fatigue Blurry vision Numbness or tingling in the feet or hands Sores that do not heal Losing weight without trying But it's important to know that your symptoms may vary, depending on which type you have: The symptoms of type 1 diabetes usually come on quickly and can be severe."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "With type 2 diabetes, the symptoms often develop slowly, over several years."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "The symptoms can be so mild that you might not even notice them."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Gestational diabetes often has no symptoms."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "If you do have symptoms, they may be mild."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "If you are pregnant, you will usually be screened for this condition between 24 and 28 weeks of pregnancy."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "To find out if you have diabetes, your health care provider will use one or more glucose blood tests ."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "There are several types, including the A1C test ."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Treatment for diabetes involves managing your blood glucose levels: If you have type 1 diabetes, you will need to take daily doses of insulin, either by injection or through a special pump."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Some people also need to take another type of diabetes medicine that works with insulin."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "If you have type 2 diabetes, you may be able to manage or even reverse it by making lifestyle changes ."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "These include eating a healthy diet , staying at healthy weight , and getting regular physical activity ."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Some people also need to take diabetes medicines to manage their diabetes."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "If you have gestational diabetes, you may be able to lower your glucose levels by eating a healthy diet and getting regular exercise."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "But be sure to talk to your provider about your treatment options."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Gestational diabetes usually goes away after you give birth."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "But you will have a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes later."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "Checking your blood glucose levels is also an important part of managing your diabetes."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "Ask your provider about the best way to check your blood glucose level and how often you should check it."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "You may be able to delay or prevent type 2 diabetes through the same lifestyle changes that are used to manage diabetes (eating a healthy diet, staying at a healthy weight, and getting regular physical activity)."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "These lifestyle changes may also help prevent gestational diabetes ."}, {"id": "S055", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-3056", "title": "Gastroenteritis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the lining of the stomach and intestines."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The main symptoms include vomiting and diarrhea ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It is usually not serious in healthy people, but it can sometimes lead to dehydration or cause severe symptoms."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "There can be many different causes of gastroenteritis: Viruses Bacteria Parasites Chemicals Reactions to certain medicines and food Viral gastroenteritis is the most common type."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It can be caused by many different viruses, including noroviruses and rotaviruses ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Some people call viral gastroenteritis the \"stomach flu.\" But this name is not medically correct."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The flu is a respiratory infection that affects your nose, throat and lungs."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "When gastroenteritis is caused by consuming foods or drinks contaminated with viruses, bacteria, parasites, or chemicals, this is called food poisoning ."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The viruses, bacteria, and parasites that cause gastroenteritis can also spread from person to person."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "You could be infected when you touch something that has the germs on it and then touch your eyes, mouth, or nose."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "What are the symptoms of gastroenteritis?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "The symptoms of gastroenteritis include: Diarrhea Pain or cramping in your abdomen (belly) Nausea Vomiting Sometimes fever Gastroenteritis is usually not serious."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "But it can sometimes cause lead to dehydration or cause severe symptoms."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Certain people are at higher risk for these problems."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "They include: Pregnant women Older adults People with weakened immune systems or other serious health conditions Infants Babies who were born prematurely or have other health conditions If you or a family member are at higher risk and have symptoms of gastroenteritis, contact a health care provider right away."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Even if you are not at high risk, it is possible to become dehydrated or have more serious symptoms."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "There are some warning signs to watch for."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It's important to contact a provider right away if you or your child have any of them: For adults, they include: Change in mental state, such as irritability or lack of energy Diarrhea lasting more than 2 days High fever Vomiting often Six or more loose stools in a day Severe pain in the abdomen (belly) or rectum Stools that are black and tarry or contain blood or pus Symptoms of dehydration, such as thirst, dry mouth , headache, dark-colored urine, and urinating less than normal For infants and children, they include: Change in the child's mental state, such as irritability or lack of energy Diarrhea lasting more than a day Any fever in infants High fever in older children Frequent loose stools Vomiting often Severe pain in the abdomen (belly) or rectum Signs or symptoms of dehydration, such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying Stools that are black and tarry or contain blood or pus How is gastroenteritis diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "To find out if you have gastroenteritis, your provider: Will do a physical exam Will ask about your symptoms May do tests of your stool What are the treatments for gastroenteritis?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Usually, people with gastroenteritis get better on their own, with rest and plenty of fluids and electrolytes ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Your provider may suggest that you take a probiotic."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Studies suggest that some probiotics may help shorten a case of diarrhea."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "People with more severe symptoms may need medicines to control nausea or vomiting."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Providers may also give other medicines for certain types of gastroenteritis, such as antibiotics for some bacterial types and antiparasitic medicines for some parasitic types."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Gastroenteritis cannot always be prevented."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "But proper hand washing , cleaning surfaces that may be infected with germs, and safe food preparation may help prevent some of the infections that can cause gastroenteritis."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There are vaccines for infants to protect against rotavirus infections."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-275", "title": "Health Statistics", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Health statistics are numbers that summarize information related to health."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Researchers and experts from government, private, and non-profit agencies and organizations collect health statistics."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They use the statistics to learn about public health and health care."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Some of the types of statistics include: How many people in the country have a disease or how many people got the disease within a certain period of time How many people of a certain group have a disease."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The groups could be based on location, race, ethnic group, sex, age, profession, income level, or level of education."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "This can help identify health disparities ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Whether a treatment is safe and effective How many people were born and died."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "How many people have access to and use health care The quality and efficiency of our health care system Health care costs, including how much the government, employers, and individuals pay for health care."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It could include how poor health can affect the country economically The impact of government programs and policies on health Risk factors for different diseases."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "An example would be how air pollution can raise your risk of lung diseases Ways to lower risk for diseases, such as exercise and weight loss to lower the risk of getting type 2 diabetes Numbers on a graph or in a chart may seem straightforward, but that's not always the case."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "It's important to be critical and consider the source."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "If needed, ask questions to help you understand the statistics and what they are showing."}]}, {"id": "MLP-533", "title": "Vascular Diseases", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your vascular system is your body's network of blood vessels."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It includes your: Arteries, which carry oxygen-rich blood from your heart to your tissues and organs Veins, which carry the blood and waste products back to your heart Capillaries, which are tiny blood vessels that connect your small arteries to your small veins."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The walls of the capillaries are thin and leaky, to allow for an exchange of materials between your tissues and blood."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Vascular diseases are conditions which affect your vascular system."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some types include: Aneurysm - a bulge or \"ballooning\" in the wall of an artery Atherosclerosis - a disease in which plaque builds up inside your arteries."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Plaque is made up of fat, cholesterol, calcium, and other substances found in the blood."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Blood clots , including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism Coronary artery disease and carotid artery disease , diseases that involve the narrowing or blockage of an artery."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The cause is usually a buildup of plaque."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Raynaud phenomenon - a disorder that causes the blood vessels to narrow when you are cold or feeling stressed Stroke - a serious condition that happens when blood flow to your brain stops."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Varicose veins - swollen, twisted veins that you can see just under the skin Vasculitis - inflammation of the blood vessels What causes vascular diseases?"}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The causes of vascular diseases depend on the specific disease."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "These causes include: Genetics Heart diseases such as high cholesterol and high blood pressure Infection Injury Medicines, including hormones Sometimes the cause is unknown."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The risk factors for vascular diseases can vary, depending on the specific disease."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "But some of the more common risk factors include: Age - your risk of some diseases goes up as you get older Conditions that can affect the heart and blood vessels, such as diabetes or high cholesterol Family history of vascular or heart diseases Infection or injury that damages your veins Lack of exercise Obesity Pregnancy Sitting or standing still for long periods of time Smoking What are the symptoms of vascular diseases?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The symptoms for each disease are different."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "To make a diagnosis, your health care provider will do a physical exam and ask about your symptoms and medical history."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "You may have imaging tests and/or blood tests."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Which treatment you get depends on which vascular disease you have and how severe it is."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Types of treatments for vascular diseases include: Lifestyle changes, such as eating a heart-healthy diet and getting more exercise Medicines, such as blood pressure medicines , blood thinners , cholesterol medicines , and clot-dissolving drugs."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "In some cases, providers use a catheter to send medicine directly to a blood vessel."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Non-surgical procedures, such as angioplasty , stenting, and vein ablation Surgery Can vascular diseases be prevented?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "There are steps you can take to help prevent vascular diseases: Make healthy lifestyle changes, such as eating a heart-healthy diet and getting more exercise Don't smoke."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "If you are already a smoker, talk to your health care provider for help in finding the best way for you to quit ."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Keep your blood pressure and cholesterol in check If you have diabetes, control your blood sugar Try not to sit or stand for up long periods of time."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "If you do need to sit all day, get up and move around every hour or so."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "If you are traveling on a long trip, you can also wear compression stockings and regularly stretch your legs."}]}]
